title: Exploring the property space of periodic cellular structures based on crystal networks
authors: Thomas S. Lumpe, Tino Stankovic
summary: Catalog of periodic truss lattices decoded from the RCSR and EPINET crystal-net databases, with effective elastic properties from periodic Euler-Bernoulli beam FE homogenization at 1% relative density. Source of our dataset family (confirmed indirectly by Indurkar 2022 and Grega 2024, which both cite this catalog; the catalog count printed in the methods, 17,087, differs from our 17,262 and from Indurkar 17,201).
relevance_to_project: Defines labels: E_s = 1 MPa, nu_s = 0.3, rho_rel = 0.01, circular struts, Euler-Bernoulli beams. Scaling n and C: the main text refers to the SI for the fit, so fitting procedure is unverified here. Exclusion of very small members documented only as one sentence in Methods.

title: Predicting deformation mechanisms in architected metamaterials using GNN
authors: Padmeya Prashant Indurkar, Sri Karlapati, Angkur Jyoti Dipanka Shaikeea, Vikram S. Deshpande
summary: Message-passing GNN (convolution + GRU, pooling, MLP) on the periodic lattice graph of the Lumpe-Stankovic catalog, classifying stretching vs bending (scaling exponent n_x) rather than regressing moduli. Independently confirms catalog properties: rho_rel = 0.01, Es = 1 MPa, nu_s = 0.3, E_i = Es C_i rho^n_i.
relevance_to_project: Closest published precursor to our GNN: same dataset, periodic edges to neighbouring cells, edge features length, radius, direction cosines. Validation accuracy 81.8% vs 95.2% train (random 90:10 split), a baseline for the n classification only, not for stiffness.

evidence.claim: Dataset: 17,201 lattices from the open catalog; rho_rel = 0.01, Es = 1 MPa, nu_s = 0.3
evidence.quote: comprises of 17,201 unique 3D lattice topologies adopted from an open-source catalogue

evidence.claim: Scaling law and exponent interpretation
evidence.quote: Ei = ES Ci rho^ni ... stretching dominated behaviour for ni ~ 1, bending dominated for ni ~ 2 (extracted text garbled; paraphrased)

evidence.claim: Periodic edges connect boundary nodes to neighbouring cells; edge features length, radius, direction cosines
evidence.quote: We connect the nodes on the outer peripheral faces of the lattice unit cell to the nodes in the neighbouring unit cells

evidence.claim: Random 90:10 split; validation accuracy 81.8%, train 95.2%
evidence.quote: accuracy achieved on the validation dataset is 81.8%

title: Energy-conserving equivariant GNN for elasticity of lattice architected metamaterials
authors: Ivan Grega, Ilyes Batatia, Gabor Csanyi, Sri Karlapati, Vikram S. Deshpande
summary: MACE-based SE(3)-equivariant GNN predicting the full 21-component stiffness tensor (via 6x6 Mandel matrix) with a positive semi-definite output layer; trained on a dataset derived from Lumpe-Stankovic with nodal perturbations and FE at 3 relative densities. Compared with CGC and NNConv baselines.
relevance_to_project: Most important baseline on a derived version of our dataset. Shows equivariance helps, PSD layer costs some accuracy, and learned penalties do not fix negative eigenvalues. Error metrics are in their own L_comp units (defined in appendix, not read), so they cannot be compared with log10 modulus errors.

evidence.quote: reduces the dataset size to 8954 base lattices

evidence.claim: Nodal perturbation augmentation, 635,454 geometries, FE at 3 relative densities; train 7000 base lattices, val/test 1296; test uses 0.1 perturbation (OOD)
evidence.quote: Thus, testing is done on OOD data.

evidence.claim: Table 1: MACE L_comp 3.88 vs CGC 8.37 (CGC+tr 4.47); MACE predicts negative eigenvalues for 30% of lattices without PSD layer, 0% with it (L_comp 3.61)
evidence.quote: The base MACE model trained on the data predicts negative eigenvalues for 30% of lattices

evidence.claim: Matrix-square A^2 PSD function gave best results; PSD enforcement slightly raises error versus unconstrained
evidence.quote: the matrix square method, A2, achieves most favourable results

evidence.claim: Dataset eigenvalues all positive; zero eigenvalue would be a mechanism

evidence.quote: all these models are 3 orders of magnitude faster than FE calculation

evidence.claim: Dual-graph representation gave no gain on this data; Lmax = 4 needed for 4th-order tensor
evidence.quote: We do not observe any performance gain from using dual graph representation on our data

title: Neural Network Layers for Prediction of Positive Definite Elastic Stiffness Tensors
authors: Charles F. Jekel, Kenneth E. Swartz, Daniel A. White, Daniel A. Tortorelli, Seth E. Watts
summary: Compares Cholesky and eigendecomposition transformation layers that force predicted homogenized 6x6 stiffness matrices to be symmetric positive definite; tests on Isotruss lattice datasets. Shows that plain regression does not guarantee SPD output.
relevance_to_project: Our targets are 9 orthotropic engineering constants; positive definiteness of the assembled orthotropic C requires E, G > 0 (guaranteed by predicting log10) plus a Poisson-coupling stability condition, which Jekel-style layers address for the full matrix.

evidence.claim: Fitting to SPD data does not guarantee SPD predictions; layers enforce SPD; one layer improves average accuracy
evidence.quote: Fitting a model to SPD data does not guarantee the model’s predictions will remain SPD.

evidence.quote: One hundred random Latin hypercube samples were performed
